issues.description: setuptools<82 cap leaks from a CI workaround into the published core package's runtime dependencies
issues.detail: The CI breakage is incidental — pkg_resources removal in setuptools 82 broke mmcv build, not autogluon runtime. Pinning setuptools<82 in core/setup.py complects a transient CI/build concern with the package's published dependency contract. Every downstream user now inherits a ceiling unrelated to their problem. Keep the cap in CI scripts where it belongs.

issues.description: mmengine/mmdet/mmcv versions and the setuptools cap are scattered across three files with no single source of truth
issues.detail: The same incidental constraint (setuptools<82) now lives in env_setup.sh, setup_mmcv.sh, and core/setup.py. The mm* version matrix lives only in setup_mmcv.sh. When the upstream issue is fixed, the revert requires hunting three places — a place-oriented bookkeeping problem. One named constant or one script.

issues.description: --no-build-isolation silently shifts mmcv's build-time deps onto whatever the ambient env happens to have
issues.detail: Disabling build isolation makes the build depend on the prior pip install setuptools<82 line executing in the same environment, in that order. The time-ordering is implicit. If anyone reorders these lines or splits them across steps, the build breaks in a confusing way. A comment stating the ordering invariant would make the implicit explicit.

issues.description: FIXME comments point at the symptom issue but not at the revert recipe
issues.detail: Both FIXMEs reference mmcv issue 3325 but don't say what to revert to. The prior state — mim install plus a pinned mmengine git SHA — is now only recoverable from git history. A one-line note ("revert to: mim install mmcv==2.1.0; pip install mmengine@<sha>") keeps the rollback cheap.

review.summary: The diff is a reasonable incidental-complexity patch for an upstream breakage, but it complects a CI build-time constraint (setuptools<82, needed because mmcv's build still imports pkg_resources) with the published runtime dependency contract of core/autogluon. That's the main thing to fix: keep the cap in the CI scripts, not in setup.py. Secondary concern is that the same workaround is now duplicated in three places with no single revert point, and --no-build-isolation makes an implicit ordering invariant load-bearing. The change itself is EASY-NOT-SIMPLE — familiar pin-and-move-on pattern — and acceptable as a temporary unblock, provided the runtime leak is reverted and the revert path is documented.
